thingsToDo.standardCall: You can combine a museum visit, lunch in the centre, Budolfi Cathedral, and a waterfront loop on a typical six-to-eight-hour call. Check opening times before you commit, and start your return well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: With eight hours or more, consider Lindholm Høje or a second museum only if you have confirmed bus or taxi timings and a clear path back. On overnight calls, reconfirm reboarding rules with the ship.

portInfo.description: The three headline cultural stops explain different parts of Abu Dhabi. The Grand Mosque is an active place of worship with visitor conduct rules; Qasr Al Hosn interprets the city’s earlier life; the Louvre offers a museum visit on Saadiyat. Each deserves time rather than being reduced to a car-window photograph. Arrival is through Zayed Port. The passenger terminal dates to 2015, Marsa Mina was developed in 2019, and Cruise Terminal 2 opened in Q4 2022. Sir Bani Yas Cruise Beach belongs to the emirate’s western island coast, not this city’s cruise-terminal inventory.

portInfo.description: Alanya occupies a fortified peninsula on Türkiye’s Mediterranean Riviera. MedCruise summarises the destination as a Turkish city of about 100,000 people that attracts about 2.5 million tourists annually, with Turkish lira as the official currency and euros and US dollars widely accepted in tourist zones. The same MedCruise port page notes that Alanya Castle, the historic dockyard and the Red Tower were added to the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List in 2009, and that cruise passengers arriving at Alanya Cruise Port can visit these attractions. ALİDAŞ Alanya Liman İşletmesi operates the cruise passenger terminal. The operator site describes a terminal dedicated to cruise ships and the Kyrenia–Alanya fast ferry service, with ISPS alignment since August 2004, a cruise quay of 533 metres, a maximum draught of 8.5 metres, and simultaneous capacity for six ships. MedCruise’s technical block lists a maximum ship length of 300 metres, no width limit, a draught of 8.5 metres, six quays totalling 966 metres, quay depths between 5 and 15 metres, one passenger terminal, anchorage, tugs and ship’s tenders allowed. Those two quay-length figures (533 m vs 966 m) are left unreconciled in this guide; both are primary-sourced and may describe different measuring conventions. Beyond the walkable harbour, classical sites at Side, Aspendos and Perge appear in both the operator kilometre table and MedCruise’s minute table. They are coach-day destinations, not walk-off sights. A separate marina with 287 yacht berths plus leisure facilities is noted by MedCruise and should not be confused with the cruise passenger terminal.

portInfo.description: Founded by Alexander in 331 BC, Alexandria became the seat of Ptolemaic rule. The Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities explains its later Roman and Byzantine urban remains, including Kom el-Dikka’s theatre, baths and lecture spaces. The modern Bibliotheca is a library-and-museum cultural complex, not the surviving ancient library. Keeping those periods distinct makes a more rewarding visit than a generic “Egypt highlights” drive. The important shore-day choice is local Alexandria versus Cairo/Giza. Neither a cruise-terminal berth total nor the physical possibility of a highway journey proves that the latter fits your all-aboard. This guide prioritises local routes with a generous vehicle return. A distant trip needs the line’s dated excursion duration and delay policy.

Bibliotheca Alexandrina, eastern Corniche: allow 90 minutes for a selective library/cultural-complex visit; check which galleries and museums are open and ticketed.
Kom el-Dikka, central Alexandria: about 90 minutes for the open-air Roman/Byzantine remains, including theatre, baths and mosaics. Sun and uneven paths matter; no unverified accessibility guarantee.
Kom al-Shoqafa catacombs, near the Serapeum: about 75 minutes for the funerary complex; steps/underground access should be checked before booking.
Serapeum/Diocletian’s Column, Alexandria: around 60 minutes; this is the monument popularly called Pompey’s Pillar, with the correct historical identification retained.

portInfo.description: The port’s aqua zone makes a useful fallback when you want to stay close to the ship, while Puerto Plata offers a fort, museum and civic square for a more cultural visit. The official map labels taxis/pre-arranged tours at point 9; it is stronger wayfinding evidence than a generic “Puerto Plata port” map pin. It does not establish named berth faces or an exact passenger entrance coordinate. Damajagua is a separate guided outing involving forest walking, sliding/jumping and water conditions. The destination authority says many trips use seven falls rather than all 27 and gives about an hour from Puerto Plata city, not from this cruise terminal. A city drive and waterfall transfer are therefore not collapsed into one optimistic time. The cable car appears in destination marketing, but present operation was not checked and it is excluded from the plans.

thingsToDo.intro: Downtown calls usually use Passenger Terminal Amsterdam (PTA) on the IJ. Some itineraries use outlying options such as IJmuiden—confirm before planning a walk.
topThings: Rijksmuseum, Museumstraat 1: allow 2–3 hours for a focused art visit. Book an entry time. The museum describes metro 52 to Vijzelgracht followed by less than ten minutes walking; confirm the terminal-to-station connection separately.

Anne Frank House, entrance Westermarkt 20: allow 60–90 minutes. Admission is time-specific and online. The official page gives about one hour inside and warns of steep stairs, limited luggage space and no photography. It also reports no tram to Westermarkt from February 2025 to February 2028.

National Maritime Museum, Kattenburgerplein 1: allow two hours. The museum describes a 19-minute walk from Centraal. Galleries have lift access; the replica ship is only partly accessible. Check individual exhibit closures.

NEMO, Oosterdok 2: allow two hours for a family science visit. Its route page gives 15 minutes walking from Centraal and directs visitors to current journey planners. Check admission and access for the intended visit; rooftop availability is not assumed.

Royal Palace, Dam Square: allow 60–90 minutes when open to visitors. It remains an official reception palace, with an opening calendar subject to change. Do not treat the building's presence on Dam as guaranteed interior access.

The port website’s technical page genuinely names the local five berths; unrelated template capacity blocks are not taken as Antiguan engineering facts. The destination’s landmark article uses a constructed tourist narrative, which is not a real traveller review and is not reproduced as one.

These are nearby alternatives when a museum is shut, not evidence that all interior spaces are open to any visitor. portInfo.description: Dover makes its geography visible immediately: a working Channel harbour below a castle and chalk cliffs. Yet a sea view is not a safe pedestrian route. The port, town and cliff-top visitor facilities sit at different levels, so plan a permitted port exit and the uphill transfer before booking an attraction. One substantial castle visit often works better than trying to collect distant Kent sights on the same day. This is an editorial recommendation, not an operator excursion promise.

topThings: Dover Castle, Castle Hill: allow about three hours for a focused visit rather than promising every tunnel and exhibition. Check the exact date's opening and access provisions; a hilltop castle is not automatically a step-free attraction.

White Cliffs visitor centre, Langdon Cliffs, Upper Road: allow 60–90 minutes for a short nearby cliff-top walk and break. Stay on official paths and away from edges. The current page says Fan Bay Deep Shelter and Emplacement are closed until March 2027; do not include them in a winter itinerary.
Dover Museum, Market Square: allow an hour for a town-centre indoor option. The municipal page gives different summer and winter Sunday arrangements; check the actual visit date.
Roman Painted House, New Street: allow 45 minutes only when reopening is confirmed. Its current winter closure makes it a future candidate, not a reliable November 2026 stop.

South Foreland Lighthouse, St Margaret's Bay: treat this as a separate extended coastal outing, not a quick addition from the cruise pier. The current official notice says the tower, tearoom, shop and toilets are closed for winter, reopening in March. There is no direct vehicular access: the National Trust describes a two-mile walk from the White Cliffs visitor centre. Confirm reopening, access and return route before setting out. A 90-minute site allowance excludes the substantial approach walk. Exact approach and transfer timing remain unresolved.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: For seven hours, allow 45 minutes to Dover Castle, 180 minutes visiting, 45 minutes for lunch and 45 minutes returning. The remaining 105 minutes is the ship buffer and recovery margin. This deliberately omits the cliffs and London. Book only after the castle calendar and ship arrival window fit together.
thingsToDo.longerCall: For nine hours, reserve 45 minutes to the castle, 150 minutes visiting, 45 minutes for lunch, 45 minutes to the White Cliffs visitor centre, 90 minutes for a short path outing and 60 minutes back. Keep 105 minutes for the ship. Transfers are conservative editorial allowances requiring independent route QA. In poor weather, use a longer castle visit or town museum instead of the cliff segment. thingsToDo.practicalTip: The cliffs visible from the ship are not the visitor-centre entrance. Save Upper Road for the National Trust arrival point and confirm the passenger gate before judging any route from its apparent distance.

portInfo.description: Dubai’s appeal is the contrast between a trading city around the Creek and newer skyline districts further along the coast. Al Fahidi’s narrow lanes, an abra crossing and Deira’s Gold Souk offer a different day from an observation deck above Downtown or Palm Jumeirah. The official 2026 city guide documents these distinct clusters. Do not spend a four-hour call trying to collect all of them. Mina Rashid has offered homeporting since 2007. Dubai Harbour’s twin-terminal arrival infrastructure began welcoming passengers in 2021. The city and terminal-logistics catalog records remain separate research obligations, even though the latter currently redirects to this city page.

topThings: Creek abra crossing, specifically Bur Dubai Abra Station–Deira Old Souq Abra Station: RTA confirms the route. Allow 45 minutes including finding the jetty, waiting and crossing. Check assistance before choosing a low-sided traditional boat; it is not automatically wheelchair accessible.

Gold Souk, Deira: a market visit rather than a promised bargain; allow 60 minutes after the crossing, with walking time between the landing and market. Use Deira Old Souq Abra Station as an agreed pickup rendezvous, with the market walking leg kept inside the visit allowance.
Burj Khalifa observation decks, Downtown Dubai: allow two hours including ticket and lift queues, plus terminal transfers. Choose a timed slot with slack; a ticket does not secure a return taxi.

The View at The Palm, Palm Jumeirah: a more geographically coherent observation-deck choice from Harbour. Allow 90 minutes and use the venue’s entrance directions rather than a pin on the whole island.

Marina Walk marine-station waterfront, Dubai Marina: a defined starting point for a 60–90-minute promenade/refreshment break, convenient as a Harbour-area option. RTA lists Marina Walk and other Marina stops; do not assume a fixed boat departure without checking its timetable.

thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Your driver needs “Port Rashid T2/T3” or “Dubai Harbour A/B”, plus the ship name. A map result for “Cruise Terminal” is not enough, especially while HBM’s entrance pin remains unresolved.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Edinburgh Castle, The Esplanade, EH1 2NG: allow two hours for selected highlights. Budget 75 minutes from Hawes Pier including waiting and the uphill approach. Book only a compatible slot; the operator warns of limited coach access and restricted parking.
Palace of Holyroodhouse, Canongate, EH8 8DX: allow 90 minutes plus 75–90 minutes from the pier. Check the working palace's calendar. Some historic rooms have access restrictions.

National Museum of Scotland, Chambers Street, EH1 1JF: allow 90 minutes plus 75–90 minutes from the pier. General admission is free; special exhibitions may cost extra. Lifts and ramps make it a useful indoor alternative, not a promise that every party can tour at the same speed.

Royal Yacht Britannia, Ocean Drive, EH6 6JJ: allow two hours, with a provisional 90–120-minute public-transport transfer from Hawes Pier. Visitor access is through Ocean Terminal's second floor. It is a separate Leith outing, not an easy extra after every old-town visit.

South Queensferry waterfront, Hawes Pier/Newhalls Road: allow an hour for a slow shore walk,10–20 minutes from the landing. Stay within the public shore route and return to the designated tender area, not another sightseeing-boat queue.
thingsToDo.shortCall: For five hours starting after landing at Hawes Pier, keep the day local:20 minutes out,60 minutes for waterfront views,45 minutes for lunch,60 minutes exploring nearby streets and 15 minutes back. Preserve 100 minutes for tender queue/recovery. This totals 300 minutes and avoids committing a short tender call to central-city admissions. Shorten the walk in poor conditions.
thingsToDo.standardCall: For seven hours from Hawes Pier, allow 75 minutes to the castle via X99/George Street and walking,120 minutes inside,45 minutes for lunch,30 minutes around the upper Royal Mile and 75 minutes back. Retain 75 minutes before the advertised last-tender deadline. Total 420 minutes. If the actual tender landing is delayed or the castle slot does not fit, replace the interior with a city walk rather than borrowing the return buffer.
thingsToDo.longerCall: For nine hours, allow 75 minutes outward,120 minutes at the castle,45 minutes for lunch,30 minutes walking through the old town towards Chambers Street,90 minutes at the museum and 75 minutes back. Keep 105 minutes before the last tender:540 minutes total. This does not also include Holyroodhouse or Britannia. An overnight still needs confirmed tender/reboarding arrangements; it is not permission to return whenever buses finish.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: These windows run from arrival ashore to the announced final-tender deadline, not from the ship's anchorage arrival to sailing time. Subtract any earlier last-tender requirement first. None of the buffers guarantees safe return if the ship changes landing operations.

Under a June 2017 35-year concession, AD Ports Group’s Fujairah Terminals upgraded container/general-cargo infrastructure and states it provides Cruise Ship services alongside RoRo and livestock. Terminal capacity targets cited by the authority include 720,000 TEUs and 1.3 million tons of general cargo by 2030. portInfo.description: Istanbul sits on the Bosphorus and works as both a marquee Mediterranean call and a growing homeport. For cruise passengers, the practical question is which berth and terminal entrance your ship uses today and how much time you have before all-aboard. Most large ships use Galataport İstanbul on the Karaköy waterfront—an underground cruise terminal where passport control, customs, and luggage handling sit below the promenade. When paperwork says Galataport, Istanbul cruise port, or the Meclis-i Mebusan address, that is the same modern complex—not a distant industrial port. Confirm with your cruise line if your booking lists another pier name (for example Salıpazarı or Sarayburnu on busy days). SeaDays does not assign berths. Istanbul is normally a dockside call at Galataport; do not assume a tender day unless your ship announces one.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Schifffahrtsmuseum Fischhalle, Wall 65: allow 60–90 minutes for maritime history. The current municipal page contains conflicting closure notices, one until 4 December and another 11 November–2 December, without consistent year labels. Treat interior access as unresolved until rechecked; use the exterior waterfront if closed. The page documents an automatic entrance door and wheelchair toilet.

Stadtmuseum Warleberger Hof, Dänische Straße 19: allow an hour for city history in the former aristocratic house. The city lists Tuesday–Sunday hours; holidays may differ. The entrance is level, but paving is partly cobbled and the exhibitions are not described as fully accessible.

St. Nikolai, Alter Markt: allow 30 minutes for art and quiet time, subject to services. The church publishes weekday and Saturday visiting hours and warns that volunteer staffing can cause unexpected closures.

Kiellinie: allow 60–90 minutes along the western waterfront, turning back according to your clock rather than walking its full length. Ferry timetables differ between summer and winter; no ferry departure is assumed here.

Alter Botanischer Garten, Schwanenweg 14: allow 45–60 minutes for a green-space extension to the promenade. Admission conditions, slopes and current opening hours need a further official check; do not present it as a guaranteed step-free option.
thingsToDo.shortCall: For five hours from Terminal 27 or 28, allow 20 minutes to the old town, 45 minutes around Alter Markt and St. Nikolai, 60 minutes at Warleberger Hof when open, 45 minutes for lunch, 40 minutes along the waterfront and 15 minutes back. The remaining 75 minutes is the ship-return buffer. If the museum is closed, substitute an outdoor stroll. For a five-hour Ostuferhafen alternative, reserve 60 minutes outward to Alter Markt, 45 minutes around St. Nikolai and the square, 30 minutes for lunch, 30 minutes for nearby old-town walking, 60 minutes returning and a 75-minute ship buffer. Drop Warleberger Hof entirely. This requires a confirmed direct organised transfer or taxi, not an unverified bus connection.
thingsToDo.standardCall: For seven hours from Ostuferhafen 1, reserve 60 minutes each way for a confirmed direct taxi or organised transfer between Ostuferhafen 1 and Alter Markt drop-off, 75 minutes at Warleberger Hof, 30 minutes at St. Nikolai, 60 minutes on the Kiellinie and 45 minutes for lunch. The remaining 90 minutes is a return buffer. From Ostseekai, the saved transfer time can support a Fischhalle visit only after its closure conflict is resolved. The Warleberger Hof block includes walking from Alter Markt; the Kiellinie block includes its connecting walk. If the actual drop-off is Hauptbahnhof instead, this precise plan needs extra walking time and a shorter promenade visit. Do not assume a bus dropped you at Alter Markt.
thingsToDo.longerCall: For nine hours from Ostseekai, allow 30 minutes to the garden, 60 minutes there, 75 minutes on the Kiellinie, 60 minutes for lunch, 90 minutes at Fischhalle if confirmed open, 30 minutes at St. Nikolai, 45 minutes for connecting walks and 30 minutes back. Leave 120 minutes for the ship. If Fischhalle is closed, use Warleberger Hof and a longer break. An overnight allows a later waterfront meal only after reboarding arrangements are confirmed.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Read the berth number as well as the port name. LP27 and LP28 mean Ostseekai, LP1 means Ostuferhafen, and LP26 appears for smaller ships at Sartorikai. A generic taxi request for the cruise terminal can therefore be ambiguous.

portInfo.description: La Romana’s cruise facility is a privately operated river-mouth terminal run by Central Romana Corporation, which also owns the historic sugar industrial complex. The operator’s technical sheet distinguishes a West Berth (sugar/molasses) from an East Berth used exclusively for cruise ships, with published pier length 256 m and maximum ship dimensions 360 × 61 m and 226,000 GT, channel entrance 11.5 m and maximum draft 10.5 m, 24/7 operations, and ISPS certification coded DOLRM / DOLRM-0001 (certificate dated 26 May 2006). Marketing pages position the port as both a port of call and a homeport with integrated transfers to La Romana International Airport (LRM), claiming ~45 minutes to Punta Cana and ~90 minutes to Santo Domingo. Cruise operations at Catalina Island (from 1992 with Costa) and the East Berth cruise pier (from 2002) are part of the same corporate story — for SeaDays mapping, keep la-romana-dominican-republic on the river terminal unless a separate Catalina slug is confirmed.

Fort Fincastle, Fort Fincastle, Bennett’s Hill, Nassau: A compact fort/harbour-view stop paired with the staircase. Allow about 45 minutes (editorial estimate). Confirm interior admission; the hill is not a flat accessible walk.

Pompey Museum of Slavery and Emancipation, Vendue House, downtown Nassau waterfront: A serious cultural-history stop close to the port. Allow about 75 minutes (editorial estimate). Current museum hours/tickets must fit the visit.

National Art Gallery of The Bahamas, Villa Doyle, Nassau: Bahamian art rather than another duty-free shop. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Check gallery schedule and the sloping approach.

Junkanoo Beach, Junkanoo Beach, west of downtown Nassau: A convenient urban waterfront break. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Swimming is conditional on current sea quality, lifeguards and weather; do not assume beach services are included.

portInfo.description: San Juan’s forts make sense when read together: El Morro defended the sea approach and San Cristóbal the land approach. A cathedral, city gate and civic square add context without requiring a rainforest coach day. The official tourism article updated 25 August 2026 documents these landmarks, but its promotional “oldest city” superlative is not repeated here. The port operator describes Old San Juan for transit/luxury calls and Pan American as a major homeport district, while Pier 4 can also handle homeporting. Those are operating roles, not a promise of your ship’s assignment. Future redevelopment piers are not silently counted as currently usable cruise berths.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Castillo San Felipe del Morro, El Morro, western tip of Old San Juan: Maritime defences and open Atlantic views. Allow about 120 minutes (editorial estimate). Heat, slopes and stairs; confirm accessible portions/current NPS schedule.

Castillo San Cristóbal, San Cristóbal, eastern edge of Old San Juan: The complementary land-facing fortification. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Not a quick extra photo stop if exploring tunnels/levels.

Catedral de San Juan Bautista, Catedral de San Juan, Old San Juan: A living religious landmark within the historic street grid. Allow about 40 minutes (editorial estimate). Worship can limit visitor access; respect dress and services.

Puerta de San Juan, Puerta de San Juan, western city wall, Old San Juan: A named gate/meeting point on the old waterfront edge. Allow about 30 minutes (editorial estimate). Uneven approaches; do not confuse it with the cruise terminal gate.

Plaza de Armas, Plaza de Armas, Old San Juan town-hall square: A shaded civic-history and refreshment pause. Allow about 45 minutes (editorial estimate). Public square access does not include government interiors.

portInfo.description: St. Thomas splits large-ship calls between the VIPA Austin “Babe” Monsanto Marine Terminal in Crown Bay (Subbase) and the privately operated WICO Dock at Havensight/Long Bay. VIPA documents Crown Bay as one of two island cruise ports, with a main dock (940 ft south / 37 ft draft Oasis-capable; 940 ft north / 28 ft draft), a 435 ft adjoining dock (27 ft draft), and a small excursion dock. WICO describes century-plus ownership of the Havensight Dock and publishes schedules that label WICO versus Crown Bay berths separately. VIPA’s Charlotte Amalie Waterfront bulkhead (3,200 ft; 4–14 ft draft) handles tenders and mini-cruise ships beside downtown shopping — not Oasis-class alongside traffic. Always read the day’s pier assignment before planning a “short walk to Main Street.”

portInfo.description: The British Virgin Islands Ports Authority manages the Cyril B. Romney Tortola Pier Park cruise pier in Road Town: 1,312 feet long by 60 feet wide, re-engineered for ships up to 180,000 GRT, explicitly excluding Oasis-class vessels above 200,000 GRT, with capacity for two large ships at anchor plus pier operations (up to four ships) and an adjacent tender pier. BVIPA notes a turning basin 0.4 miles south-southeast with radius over 300 metres and minimum depth 11.3 metres, and records expansions (1994 / 1999 / 2015) plus the 15 February 2019 renaming. The landside five-acre Pier Park (11 buildings, 18 kiosks, 70+ retail units) is operated with Tortola Pier Park Ltd at Wickhams Cay I. Do not confuse the deep cruise pier with the shallower Road Town Jetty ferry facility (190 m / 3.65 m) also listed by BVIPA.

portInfo.description: Alghero (L’Alguer) is a fortified Catalan-speaking town on Sardinia’s northwest coast. The municipal tourism site (Fondazione Alghero) frames the destination around fortress walls, coral heritage, museums and the wider Capo Caccia coast, including Neptune’s Cave. Cruise passengers land in the harbour precinct; from there the historic centre is the natural walk-off loop, while Neptune’s Cave is reached by boat services that advertise departures from the port of Alghero. The Linea Grotte di Nettuno operator describes the caves as among Sardinia’s most famous, extending about 4 km with only a visitor portion open for safety, and markets daily battello (boat) links from Alghero harbour plus mini-cruises along the coral riviera. Exact 2026 seasonal timetables and ticket prices must be confirmed on the operator site or at the quay on the day — this guide does not invent slot times. Catalan Alghero’s visitor story on the municipal tourism site emphasises the fortress city, wall promenades, coral identity and museum network. That framing matters for cruise planning: the high-value walk-off sights are compact, while Neptune’s Cave is a boat-mediated add-on with weather risk. Passengers who try to force cave + full wall circuit + long lunch into a five-hour call routinely lose their buffer — the minute budgets below are deliberately conservative. Fondazione Alghero’s public contacts (tourist office phone/email and Largo Lo Quarter organisation phones) are listed so shore teams can verify day-of notices. They are not a substitute for the ship’s port agent on berthing questions.

portInfo.description: Arendal Havn places its cruise quays in the town centre of this Sørlandet harbour city, historically on seven small islands and often nicknamed the “Venice of the North” in port copy. Technical data for Batterikaien and Hotellkaien include published WGS positions, 110 m / 77 m lengths, 10 m max draught and 2.2 m quay height. Approach is through Galtesund (~4 nautical miles from the pilot), with a 120 m minimum entrance width between navigation lights. Contact +47 975 27 000 / VHF 12 or 16; post@arendalhavn.no.

portInfo.description: Bonaire’s most rewarding distinction is between its living town, cultural villages and protected landscapes. Kralendijk’s Fort Oranje and former fish market make a compact first visit; Mangazina di Rei interprets rural heritage around Rincon. The southern slave huts and navigation obelisks should be read as evidence of salt production and forced labour, not treated only as a coastal photograph. Water access is not simply “free beach equals free snorkelling”. STINAPA requires a Nature Fee for marine/national-park users; its current park page quotes a one-day cruise-passenger fee ofUS$10, read 5 November 2026, but coverage/exemptions need direct confirmation. That is a conservation charge, not proof of a government visitor-entry-tax amount. The tourism guide’s broad annual-fee summary is not substituted for the operator’s cruise-specific rule.

For a short call, one town and its nearby viewpoints are enough. The island’s Roman villas, monastic buildings and later literary connections give a culture-led visit substance beyond the shopping streets.

portInfo.description: Cartagena’s best compact route connects named places rather than promising the entire historic centre:the Clock Tower/Portal de los Dulces, San Pedro Claver and Las Bóvedas. Castillo San Felipe adds a distinct hill-fort visit outside that street circuit. Heat makes a shaded lunch and fewer paid interiors sensible. The official tourism article’s generic “on foot at any time” phrasing is not a safety guarantee or an accessible-route audit. Port Oasis occupies part of the cruise-terminal campus and limits access to arriving/embarking cruise guests. Its animal-recovery/conservation role is described by the operator, but undated animal counts are not repackaged as current wildlife statistics. Its internal location can support a short call without a traffic-dependent island excursion.

Concepción Castle sits uphill; the harbour museums and lower streets are the gentler alternative.

portInfo.description: Livorno is Tuscany's main port and one of the Mediterranean's best examples of a "gateway" call: few passengers come for Livorno itself, yet its canals, Medici fortresses and seafront Terrazza Mascagni make a pleasant low-stress day. The real decision is how far inland to go. Pisa's Field of Miracles is close and simple by train; Florence is a full commitment with two train legs, a bus or taxi and a shuttle each way. The terminal operator, Porto di Livorno 2000, runs the Alto Fondale terminal at quays 46/47, opened in 2013 for ships over 300 m.

portInfo.description: Beirut rewards a tightly focused cultural day rather than an unsupported promise to cover Lebanon from a ship. The Barakat Building’s civil-war history needs careful interpretation, not a glib photo-stop description. Those researched places do not establish that a cruise can currently discharge passengers safely. A viable day begins with a real call, approved port transport, a route-specific security decision and confirmed venue access. Keep northern/eastern city museum choices separate from districts under different warnings; this guide does not certify any route as safe based on a city label.

portInfo.description: Castaway Cay’s useful planning unit is an activity area, not a list of public monuments. These are genuine mapped places, but inclusion, staffing and water access still depend on Disney’s operating decisions. The FAQ describes a direct dock and tram service. portInfo.description: Puerto Bahías de Huatulco, under ASIPONA Salina Cruz, is described by the authority as a fundamentally tourism-oriented harbour whose operations concentrate on cruise ships and cruise passengers, marinas and local nautical tourism. The Programa Maestro de Desarrollo Portuario (PMDP) 2022–2027 details specialised cruise infrastructure: a finger pier with two berths totalling 450 m of berthing length (180 m concrete-pile platform plus two 153.10 m breasting dolphins), a passenger-and-authorities terminal building, and 9.0 m official draft on the cruise approach and basins. Cruise is named the port’s principal business line; the PMDP notes pandemic-era collapse and a 2021 movement of 18.3 thousand passengers during early recovery — treat that figure as year-specific, not a current forecast.

portInfo.description: The City of Key West Port & Marine Services describes consolidation of deep-water cruise-ship and Navy-vessel coordination and states that the Port of Key West consists of three docking facilities: Mallory Square Dock, Pier B (privately owned), and the Navy Mole. City history notes Mallory Dock was improved in 1984 into a full cruise docking facility and cites older passenger volumes (e.g., FY1999) that must not be treated as current statistics. Separately, Keys News reported on 7 May 2026 that the Navy terminated the city’s Outer Mole lease with effective date 3 August 2026, noting the Outer Mole had served large cruise ships until 2020. For SeaDays research, Mallory and Pier B remain the evidenced civilian cruise options; Outer Mole cruise availability after lease end is an explicit gap.

portInfo.description: Kahului Harbor is Maui’s principal commercial harbour. HDOT’s Kahului Harbor Development Plan describes Pier 1 as a multiple-use facility primarily used by Matson, Pasha and cruise ships, with the Pier 1 shed serving as the cruise passenger terminal and equipment storage. Cruise ships can moor at Berths 1A or 1C but are more likely to use Berth 1A to reduce conflicts with cargo; passengers using Berth 1C are separated from cargo operations by barriers and fencing. Public access uses Ala Luina Street or Perimeter Road connected to Ka‘ahumanu Avenue / Hana Highway corridors. Berth scheduling for State commercial harbours runs through Hawaii.PortCall.Com.

portInfo.description: Geiranger Port, run by Stranda Hamnevesen KF, sits deep in the UNESCO-listed Geirangerfjord with a dedicated cruise terminal concept built around the SeaWalk floating walkway, three anchorage positions, and a small fixed quay. Tender pier to centre is ~100 m / about five minutes. Stern-to at Lausneset max LOA 250 m; sway position 3S max 180 m.

portInfo.description: Half Moon Cay (Little San Salvador) is the Bahamas private-island product long associated with Holland America Line and now branded RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay. The HAL destination page frames it as a low-crowd beach day with roaming drinks carts, snorkel/kayak rentals, pickleball, Destination Dining BBQ and Lobster Shack, plus cabanas and Deluxe Beach Villas. A 10 Dec 2024 joint release with Carnival Cruise Line announces a multi-year enhancement: distinct south and north welcome plazas over more than one mile of beach, a refreshed south-side Beach Club, a newly developed north side with lunch venues/bars/tram, and a newly constructed north pier intended to allow ships to dock — including Carnival Excel-class ships visiting for the first time — with completion beginning summer 2026 and continuing through year-end. Until that pier is confirmed in service for a given sailing, treat transfer mode (tender vs alongside) as ship-day specific. This is a private / cruise-line destination, not a public ferry harbour.

portInfo.description: Ocean Cay is MSC Cruises’ exclusive Bahamas private island, restored from a former sand-excavation site into a marketed marine reserve with beaches, spa, food trucks/bars, cabanas and conservation programming. The MSC destination FAQ states ships berth directly at the quay next to the Welcome Centre in Ocean Village, so guests walk ashore without tenders, may return to the ship at any time during the call, and navigate by signed paths (about twenty minutes to the far side of the ~95-acre island). Eight named beaches (including North/South lagoon beaches, Sunset Beach, Lighthouse Bay beside the ~100-foot lighthouse, and Yacht Club-only Ocean House Beach) plus Seakers Food Court, Springer’s and Lighthouse bars, and the MSC Foundation Super Coral / Mission Blue Hope Spot story are on the same destination materials.

portInfo.description: Niedersachsen Ports describes Wilhelmshaven as Germany’s sole deep-water port on the Jade, with an outer deep-water section and an inner harbour behind a dual-chamber sea lock that is independent of the tide. The published product mix is bulk, containers (JadeWeserPort), energy/LNG and project cargo — not a cruise brochure. The NPorts Port Information Guide nonetheless lists North Harbour / Hannoverkai with max LOA 300 m, ~325 m solid quay, 11 m alongside depth at harbour normal, electricity/freshwater/Wi‑Fi and no stationary cargo gear. A 2020 city press release documented Mein Schiff 6 berthing at Hannoverkai for classification/diving works with no crew shore leave during COVID restrictions — that is evidence the quay can take a large cruise ship for technical purposes, not evidence of a regular tourist call programme.

Museo de Arte de Ponce — longer call with taxi — ~150 min.
La Guancha boardwalk — seafood lunch stop — ~90 min.
Coffee plantation / south-coast coach — long call only.
thingsToDo.shortCall: ≥4 h. One central Ponce stop (Plaza Las Delicias area) with ≥90 min tender/transport buffer if assigned anchorage.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ponce is not San Juan — keep port codes and excursion pickup points labelled Ponce on your documents.
